text:
elaine: Heads-up — onboarding client QuickCart is seeing a burst of 429s from the Browser SDK in staging. Happens immediately on page load. Logs show a big spike of OPTIONS preflight + repeated /v1/chat calls. Any ideas if this is a preflight fanout or our origin throttles?

ben: Which SDK version and how do they instantiate the client? Single instance or new per render?

elaine: js-sdk@0.9.1. They said they create a new client each time the support chat modal opens (so dozens of inits when the homepage loads for some users). Burst is ~60–120 reqs/sec for ~5–8s, then it settles and 429s stop.

ivan: That sounds like a classic preflight + client-per-component pattern. OPTIONS + Authorization headers will trigger preflight for every unique request if there's no caching. Are they setting Access-Control-Max-Age? Also are they sending Authorization on OPTIONS?

elaine: Snippet from the failing request headers:

```
:method: OPTIONS
:authority: api.redwood.example
:scheme: https
:origin: https://quickcart.example
:access-control-request-method: POST
:access-control-request-headers: authorization, content-type
:authorization: Bearer <token>
```

elaine: (ps — customer is behind a corporate proxy in some users, but repros without proxy as well)

ben: Two quick fixes we can recommend to the customer: make the SDK client a singleton (reuse across renders) and set Access-Control-Max-Age on their endpoint so the browser caches preflight. Short term server-side mitigations: increase burst allowance for their account or relax per-origin preflight counting.

ivan: Also note: browsers will include Authorization in access-control-request-headers which prevents simple requests. If we can accept unauthenticated OPTIONS (no auth header) or at least not count them against rate limit, that drastically reduces cost. We can implement internal rule: treat OPTIONS as non-rate-limited for accounts in onboarding for 24h.

elaine: Customer can’t ship a code change this week. Can we enable the temporary rule for account qc-77?

ivan: Yes — I’ll open a quick ops task to allow OPTIONS passthrough for qc-77 and bump their burst window to avoid 429s during onboarding.

ben: I’ll add an SDK quickfix doc snippet showing singleton pattern and an example: 

```js
// create once, reuse for app lifecycle
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/sdk'
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
export default client
```

ben: Also recommend setting Access-Control-Max-Age on their server (e.g., 600s) so preflights are cached.

elaine: Perfect. I’ll tell customer both: temporary server-side leniency + recommended SDK change for long-term. I’ll follow up after ops confirms the workaround. Thanks folks :heart:

deploy-bot: ops-ticket #CS-2147 created by ivan — summary: temporary OPTIONS passthrough + burst bump for account qc-77. ETA: 2h

ben: nice. once ops confirms we should cc sales for renewal risk mitigation notes.

ivan: on it, will update ticket with logs and timeline.

elaine: got it, sending guidance to QuickCart now.
